strengths: Well-motivated biological problem: clearly articulates how the brain combines generative and discriminative inference, with strong neuroscience grounding
Elegant unified energy function: naturally combines both inference pathways without ad-hoc architectural additions like stop-gradients
Biologically plausible implementation: maintains local computations, Hebbian plasticity, and interpretable neural circuit with value and error neurons
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: thorough testing across multiple datasets, learning paradigms (supervised/unsupervised/combined), and biologically-relevant tasks
Insightful mechanistic analysis: Section 4.4 provides excellent visualization of energy landscapes showing mutual regularization and superior sample quality (Inception/FID scores)
Strong robustness to occlusion: maintains ~85% accuracy with 80% missing pixels, demonstrating effective use of generative priors
Excellent reproducibility: detailed supplementary material with hyperparameters, procedures, compute times, and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: combining separate generative and discriminative energy terms is mathematically straightforward; contribution is primarily empirical demonstration rather than theoretical insight

Critical hyperparameter tuning requirement: α_disc and α_gen require task-dependent manual adjustment (αdisc >> αgen for supervised learning); energy magnitude mismatches inadequately addressed; undermines biological plausibility

Computational overhead without demonstrated advantage: doubles computational cost with two weight matrices and error neurons; 750+ hours of hyperparameter tuning per dataset; no advantage over training separate models

Problematic max-pooling interaction: grid artifacts in CIFAR-10 reconstructions (Section 4.3); removing max-pooling causes ~25% accuracy drop (Table 15); workaround (task-specific α scaling) adds complexity
Weak theoretical foundation: no convergence guarantees, no characterization of when bidirectional processing helps, no gradient flow analysis, primarily empirical energy landscape visualization

Overstated biological plausibility: task-dependent α configuration lacks biological justification; two error neurons per value neuron is significant overhead; feedforward initialization sweep unclear in brain implementation
Limited comparison scope: primarily vs discPC/genPC/hybridPC; Helmholtz machines and Symmetric Predictive Estimator only briefly mentioned; missing modern bidirectional architectures

Somewhat anticipated experimental results: multimodal bPC equivalence to unimodal bPC makes superior genPC performance unsurprising; missing information robustness follows from bPC's discriminative capabilities
Scalability concerns: largest experiments use 256-dimensional representations; extensive tuning impractical at scale; unclear applicability to ImageNet or modern deep learning

Incomplete experimental design: some results on CIFAR-10 only; missing statistical significance tests; no experiments combining occlusion robustness tests with CIFAR datasets; 600K inference steps for missing data raises realism questions

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple tasks, datasets, and architectures with extensive ablations and proper statistical testing
Elegant unified energy formulation combining discriminative and generative pathways with clear biological implementation
Strong empirical results showing bPC matches specialized models on their tasks while outperforming hybridPC, with particular robustness to missing inputs
Insightful energy landscape analysis (Section 4.4) effectively demonstrates why bPC succeeds through sharper, data-localized minima
Demonstrates scalability to deep networks (VGG-16) and addresses reproducibility with detailed hyperparameter specifications
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: the main contribution is a straightforward weighted combination of two existing energy functions without theoretical justification for why this combination is optimal

Critical dependency on fixed, manually-tuned hyperparameters (α_gen, α_disc) that require task-specific adjustment and show high sensitivity (SM D: 98.1%→87% as ratio changes), limiting practical applicability
Computational costs inadequately analyzed: paper claims energy-efficiency but requires two error signals per layer and 100+ inference steps; deep model training requires ad-hoc error optimization
Generation quality trade-offs on complex datasets: acknowledged checkerboard artifacts from max-pooling; removing pooling for clean generation reduces classification ~25% on CIFAR-10 (85%→62%)
Ad-hoc design choices undermine unified framework claim: deep models require two-stage inference (warm-up with α_disc=0), with α_gen varying from 1e-5 to 1e-8 across architectures (SM Table 23)

Baseline comparison concerns: hybridPC designed with stop-gradient operations that limit supervised performance by design; limited engagement with other bidirectional architectures beyond related work

Biological plausibility claims need strengthening: no mapping to specific cortical circuits, claim about dendritic error handling under-developed, real neural systems show asymmetries between pathways
Narrow evaluation scope: all experiments on vision tasks; no evaluation on NLP, RL, or other domains where discriminative/generative trade-offs may differ fundamentally

strengths: Well-motivated contribution addressing genuine gap in predictive coding literature; brain employs both generative and discriminative inference
Elegant theoretical framework: unified energy function (Eq. 3) naturally combines genPC and discPC rather than using ad-hoc approaches
Maintains biological plausibility with local computations and Hebbian learning rules throughout; clear neural circuit implementation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, learning settings, and architectures with rigorous baselines and statistical reporting
Strong empirical results: bPC consistently matches/exceeds unidirectional models in their domains and outperforms hybridPC across tasks
Insightful energy landscape analysis (Section 4.4) providing clear intuition for why bPC works—sharpening discriminative minima while anchoring to data via generative feedback
Exemplary reproducibility: extensive supplementary material with detailed hyperparameters, architectural specifications, ablations, and promised code release
Demonstrates effectiveness on biologically-relevant tasks (multimodal learning, inference with missing information) showing practical relevance beyond standard classification
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution of combining two energy functions is conceptually straightforward; lacks deeper theoretical insight into why this combination is optimal

Hyperparameter tuning burden undermines unified framework narrative: αgen and αdisc require task-specific tuning with significant sensitivity (Appendix D); different settings for supervised vs. unsupervised learning; no learnable scaling implemented

Computational cost largely unaddressed: missing information inference requires 600,000 steps (MNIST) or 3,000 (deep models); no timing comparisons provided; two-stage inference for deep models suggests convergence difficulties
Inconsistent performance on complex tasks: bPC achieves 85.06% on CIFAR-10 combined task vs. hybridBP's 90.11% (Table 14); reconstruction RMSE gaps remain relative to BP methods
Limited architectural scope: only VGG tested for deep models; no ResNets, modern optimizers, or ImageNet evaluation; max-pooling incompatibility requires workarounds limiting architectural choices

Biological plausibility claims need tempering: separate error neurons assumption is neurobiologically debatable; brain connection is motivational rather than validational; claims about resembling biological inference not firmly supported
Energy landscape analysis limited to toy XOR problem; unclear how insights generalize to high-dimensional spaces; real-task landscapes would be more convincing

Incomplete baseline comparisons: mentions U-Nets, VAEVAE, VAR, PredNet in related work but provides no experimental comparisons; limited comparison with other biologically plausible learning algorithms
Dense presentation with critical experimental details relegated to appendices; some choices (specific inference step counts, initialization schemes) lack justification in main text
Missing practical guidance: no decision framework for when to use bPC vs. alternatives; scalability to modern architectures undemonstrated; convergence analysis lacking
